_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 22 (the Akedah / binding of Isaac). Saadia-specific moves: v.1 'לביך' = 'I am at your service' (Arabic prayer-response formula for 'הנני' — same in v.7,11); v.2 'בלד אלעבאדה' = 'the land of worship' (Saadia interprets המוריה as 'the place of worship/service'); v.12 'ערפת אלנאס' = 'I have made [it] known to people' (Saadia: God didn't 'come to know' Abraham's fear — He made it manifest to others — anti-anthropomorphic); v.14 'אללה אלמתגלי' = 'the God who reveals Himself'.

translations.1: And it was after these things — God tested Abraham; and said to him: 'O Abraham!' He said: 'I am at your service.'
translations.2: He said: 'Take your son, your only one, whom you love — he is Isaac — and go to the land of worship; and offer him there as an offering, upon one of the mountains which I shall tell you.'
translations.3: And Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his donkey; and he took his two youths with him, and Isaac his son; and he split wood for the offering; and he arose and went to the place which God had told him.
translations.4: And on the third day, Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place from afar.
translations.5: And he said to his youths: 'Sit here with the donkey; and I and the boy will go on yonder, and we shall bow down, and we shall return to you.'
translations.6: And Abraham took the wood of the offering, and set it upon Isaac his son; and he took with him the fire and the knife; and the two of them went on together.
translations.7: And Isaac said to Abraham his father: 'O my father!' He said: 'I am at your service, my son.' He said: 'Behold the fire and the wood — but where is the lamb for the offering?'
translations.8: Abraham said: 'God shall show forth the lamb for the offering, my son.' And the two of them went on together.
translations.9: Until they came to the place which God had told him. And Abraham built there an altar; and he arranged the wood; and he bound Isaac his son, and set him upon the altar above the wood.
translations.10: Then Abraham put forth his hand, and took the knife — to slaughter his son.
translations.11: And the angel of God called to him from the sky, and said: 'O Abraham, O Abraham!' He said: 'I am at your service.'
translations.12: He said: 'Do not put forth your hand against the boy, nor do anything to him — for now I have made it known to people that you fear God, and you have not withheld your son, your only one, from me.'
translations.13: Then Abraham lifted up his eyes after that, and looked — and behold, a ram, its horns entangled in a thicket of trees. And he went and took it, and offered it as an offering in place of his son.
translations.14: And Abraham named that place 'The God who reveals Himself' — so that it would be said, on the like of this day: 'On this mountain — God reveals Himself.'
translations.15: Then the angel of God called to Abraham a second time from the sky.
translations.16: He said: 'By My name I have sworn — says God — that since you have done this thing, and not withheld your son, your only one, from Me,
translations.17: surely I shall bless you, and multiply your offspring like the stars of the sky and like the sand which is upon the shore of the sea; and your offspring shall possess the towns of its enemies.
translations.18: And in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed — recompense for that you have accepted My word.'
translations.19: Then Abraham returned to his youths; and they rose, and went together to Beer-Sheba; and Abraham settled there.
translations.20: And it was after these things, that Abraham was told, saying: 'Behold, Milkah — she too has borne sons to Nahor your brother:
translations.21: Uz his firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
translations.22: and Kesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Yidlaph, and Bethuel.'
translations.23: And Bethuel begot Rebekah. These eight Milkah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
translations.24: And his maidservant — her name was Reumah; she too bore: Tevah, and Gaham, and Tahash, and Maacah.
